items.before: updateDetails, replaceFulfilments and save each call load() (findByIdAndOwnerId), change the entity and then call repository.save(). @Version is on the entity, but the frontend client (services/templates/client.js) never sends the version back, and no endpoint accepts an expected version. The only concurrency check is whether two requests overlap inside the backend. Overlapping requests get an OptimisticLockingFailureException, which the global handler turns into 409 STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN. Requests that do not overlap silently overwrite each other, because PUT /fulfilments replaces the whole list.
items.after:
updateDetails, replaceFulfilments and save each do the same three steps:

- call load() (findByIdAndOwnerId)
- change the entity
- call repository.save()

@Version is on the entity. But the frontend client (services/templates/client.js) never sends the version back.

No endpoint accepts an expected version.

The only concurrency check is whether two requests overlap inside the backend:

- Overlapping requests get an OptimisticLockingFailureException. The global handler turns it into 409 STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN.
- Requests that do not overlap silently overwrite each other, because PUT /fulfilments replaces the whole list.

Use MongoTemplate.findAndModify with Criteria where(_id).is(id).and(ownerId).is(ownerId), and Update set(status, SAVED), so a repeated save is a no-op instead of a 409. Set 'saved' with a separate conditional update (criteria saved: null) or $min. For replaceFulfilments and updateDetails, accept the expected version (a concurrencyToken, as notifications use) and match on it, returning 409 when it is stale. Have the frontend send back the version it read and handle the 409 as notifications already do.
items.after:
Make save idempotent and atomic:

- Use MongoTemplate.findAndModify with Criteria where(_id).is(id).and(ownerId).is(ownerId), and Update set(status, SAVED). A repeated save is then a no-op instead of a 409.
- Set 'saved' with a separate conditional update (criteria saved: null) or $min.

For replaceFulfilments and updateDetails, accept the expected version (a concurrencyToken, as notifications use). Match on it, and return 409 when it is stale.

Have the frontend send back the version it read. Have it handle the 409 as notifications already do.

items.before: Holds on the branch. NotificationTemplateService.save, replaceFulfilments and updateDetails all call load() and then repository.save() on an entity that carries @Version. The frontend client (services/templates/client.js) sends no version, and no endpoint accepts one. GlobalExceptionHandler maps OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409, and check-answers saveTemplate (controller.js:286) has no catch, so an overlapping save shows an error page. The template-records port sends the full fulfilment set it loaded earlier, so the two-tab lost update is real. Three things lower the severity. Notifications' own fulfilment replace has no expected-version check either (only /copy takes a concurrencyToken), so this copies the house pattern rather than falling short of it. A double-click gap (around 100ms) is usually longer than one Mongo find-and-save, so the second save normally runs after the first and leaves the template saved. And a lost update needs the same user editing in two tabs.
items.after:
Holds on the branch.

NotificationTemplateService.save, replaceFulfilments and updateDetails all call load() and then repository.save(). The entity carries @Version.

The frontend client (services/templates/client.js) sends no version. No endpoint accepts one.

GlobalExceptionHandler maps OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409. check-answers saveTemplate (controller.js:286) has no catch. So an overlapping save shows an error page.

The template-records port sends the full fulfilment set it loaded earlier. So the two-tab lost update is real.

Three things lower the severity:

- Notifications' own fulfilment replace has no expected-version check either (only /copy takes a concurrencyToken). So this copies the house pattern rather than falling short of it.
- A double-click gap (around 100ms) is usually longer than one Mongo find-and-save. So the second save normally runs after the first and leaves the template saved.
- A lost update needs the same user editing in two tabs.

items.id: killed: Ownership rests entirely on a caller-asserted User-Id header, and organisationId is stored but never used
items.before: Refuted as a defect in this merge. (1) The 'undefined' owner scenario cannot happen: services/templates/index.js requireOwner() throws before every client call (listFor, startFor, getFor, updateDetailsFor, replaceFulfilmentsFor, saveFor) when ownerId is falsy, so the literal string 'undefined' is never sent. (2) A trusted User-Id header is the backend's existing model: NotificationController already takes HEADER_USER_ID as a required header at lines 225 and 258 without verifying it. The templates merge did not introduce it. (3) Scoping templates by user, not organisation, is the stated intent. The backlog constraint (backlog.json line 39) reads 'scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates)', and the field's Javadoc says organisationId is 'Recorded, not used to scope'. The multi-organisation case is a product question, not a bug.
items.after:
Refuted as a defect in this merge.

(1) The 'undefined' owner scenario cannot happen.

- services/templates/index.js requireOwner() throws when ownerId is falsy.
- It does this before every client call (listFor, startFor, getFor, updateDetailsFor, replaceFulfilmentsFor, saveFor).
- So the literal string 'undefined' is never sent.

(2) A trusted User-Id header is the backend's existing model.

- NotificationController already takes HEADER_USER_ID as a required header at lines 225 and 258, without verifying it.

(3) Scoping templates by user, not organisation, is the stated intent.

- The backlog constraint (backlog.json line 39) reads 'scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates)'.
- The field's Javadoc says organisationId is 'Recorded, not used to scope'.

The multi-organisation case is a product question, not a bug.

items.id: killed: An argument or workspace-lookup error no longer writes, or clears, the --result file
items.before: The regression is real. Before 664beddd, `resultPath = opts.result ? resolve(opts.result) : null` came before parseOptions, so a parse or workspace-lookup error wrote an error envelope. Now index.js:309-328 sets resultPath only after both succeed. The harmful scenario does not hold, though. Those errors make the foreground gate call exit 2 at once with the error on stdout. It is never moved to the background, so GATE_WAIT_RULE never sends the agent to gate-wait, and GATE_RULE (increment-build-loop.js:982-983) says an error before any rung is RED. The holder is always the fixed RUN_HOLDER from gateCommand, so the 'regex refuses the holder' trigger cannot come from the loop. Even before the commit, a parse failure never cleared the file. To read a stale envelope, an agent would have to break the loop's rules.
items.after:
The regression is real.

Before 664beddd, `resultPath = opts.result ? resolve(opts.result) : null` came before parseOptions. So a parse or workspace-lookup error wrote an error envelope.

Now index.js:309-328 sets resultPath only after both succeed.

The harmful scenario does not hold, though:

- Those errors make the foreground gate call exit 2 at once, with the error on stdout.
- It is never moved to the background, so GATE_WAIT_RULE never sends the agent to gate-wait.
- GATE_RULE (increment-build-loop.js:982-983) says an error before any rung is RED.
- The holder is always the fixed RUN_HOLDER from gateCommand. So the 'regex refuses the holder' trigger cannot come from the loop.
- Even before the commit, a parse failure never cleared the file.

To read a stale envelope, an agent would have to break the loop's rules.

items.id: killed: Template saves drop the concurrency token: last write wins with no stale-action check
items.before: The two-tab scenario does not happen. state.commit (engine/write/commit.js:7) loads the current record fresh on every POST and applies only that page's patch to it. Tab B's Transport save therefore merges onto the stored fulfilment, which already includes tab A's Origin change, and does not overwrite it with a stale copy. Also, replaceJourneyFulfilment prefers the same-request memo (journey.js:147-150), so notification saves send the freshly loaded version, not the tab's rendered token, and would not reject this case either. What the template port drops is protection against a true simultaneous-write race, which is narrow and not the scenario described.
items.after:
The two-tab scenario does not happen.

state.commit (engine/write/commit.js:7) loads the current record fresh on every POST. It applies only that page's patch to it.

So tab B's Transport save merges onto the stored fulfilment, which already includes tab A's Origin change. It does not overwrite it with a stale copy.

Also, replaceJourneyFulfilment prefers the same-request memo (journey.js:147-150). So notification saves send the freshly loaded version, not the tab's rendered token. They would not reject this case either.

What the template port drops is protection against a true simultaneous-write race. That is narrow, and not the scenario described.

A germinal template cannot be created today.

INS does offer Germinal products in template mode, and hands over to /templates/new?type=germinal-products. But in template-name/controller.js:

- newPost (lines 74-77) redirects to Manage templates before templates.startFor when type is germinal-products
- namePost (lines 91-94) refuses to update an existing template to germinal

No germinal template is ever stored. So no card shows a dead Use template button.

The scenario ('chooses Germinal products, saves it, then presses Use template') cannot happen.

The setId check in use-template.js is defensive and is tested.

Choosing Germinal does silently bounce back to the list. But that is a different, known deferral (req-1876), and not this finding.
